body: What would be the downside of only setting the implicit anchor element when the popover shows (including setting it to null if there's no source)?

WebKit ties the popover "implicit anchor" to the "popover trigger" concept currently, so to make it only set to null during show would effectively require that be rewritten, just as an fyi.

I'm slightly confused why the spec is only setting "implicit anchor element" to null when fireEvents is true? That seems wrong?
@lukewarlow I don't understand. What would happen if WebKit simply didn't null the "implicit anchor" on the close case.

If I understand what Luke is saying, it is that WebKit doesn't store an implicit anchor and instead resolves it to the popover trigger, instead.  From my perspective that seemed sensible, initially. Upon further investigation though it seems as though the implicit anchor steps are what cause reflow. How does WebKit handle reflow in this regard? Perhaps the issue is around reflow?

> I'm slightly confused why the spec is only setting "implicit anchor element" to null when fireEvents is true? That seems wrong?

Looks like this is wrong. Chrome removes implicit anchor association during "remove from the top layer immediately". So it would make sense for it to be step 12, not 9.5.

Yeah basically what Keith said.

WebKit doesn't store an "implicit anchor" explicitly. It has an "invoker" in PopoverData and an "invokedPopover" on Element. Implicit anchoring is keyed off of the "invokedPopover" part of Element which when updated triggers something in the style system.
If Chrome is only removing the association in cases where it's "removed from the top layer immediately", that seems ok. The spec should do the same, so 10.1?

It seems like "removed from the top layer immediately" only happens if the `popover` attribute is removed. Maybe there are a couple of other edge cases.

Ugh that boolean shouldn't be called `fireEvents` since it's just one of the things it does.

> That would still be too early for the codepen demo, right? It'd result in the Safari behaviour.

It would if we're assuming that removing the implicit anchor association is what causes reflow. However given Chrome sets the implicit anchor association more closely aligned with the spec, I am guessing it has other logic to handle when reflow should occur for implicit anchors.

I wonder if it should be part of the css spec to talk about how reflowing an implicit anchor should be delayed if an animation or transition is occurring? 

> If Chrome is only removing the association in cases where it's "removed from the top layer immediately", that seems ok. The spec should do the same, so 10.1?

If it was in 10.1 it would also need to remain in 9.5. It could be step 12 (or 11) and handle for both if fireEvents is true, or false.

Ahh I think I might know what it is, the spec is wrong.

"removed from the top layer immediately" actually gets called in both codepaths. Chrome sets implicit anchor element to null as part of those steps. Which are delayed in the case you "[Request an element to be removed from the top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#request-an-element-to-be-removed-from-the-top-layer)" 

I'm not sure WebKit actually has a distinction between these two cases, I guess because the overlay property isn't implemented outside of Chromium?

Chrome has another logic; it has the `maybe implicit anchor` which, when set, causes reflow _only_ if it's being added (not removed): https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/dom/element.cc;drc=ce651b75de646270fc28ce175bcc951842095309;bpv=0;bpt=1;l=12428

IOW when an implicit anchor is removed, Chrome intentionally skips reflow, which is likely why you're not seeing the animation bug in Chrome. I imagine WebKit triggers style invalidation whenever it changes and so runs into the situation described in OP.
I'm not 100% sure what 'reflow' means here, but ideally the popover should continue to position in relation to the button until it leaves the top layer.

It leaves the top layer immediately though, because only Chromium actually supports the overlay property which is what keeps it in the top layer for a longer period of time. This might just be a symptom of that being missing?

https://searchfox.org/wubkat/source/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLElement.cpp#1230 - WebKit might actually be removing the implicit anchor too early regardless, I think this line needs moving down to 1245 too. But because there's no overlay the behaviour is the same.

Reflow = Layout invalidation. Chrome _skips_ invalidating the layout when removing an implicit anchor, so the anchored position association is no longer there but that fact is ignored because the style engine hasn't been told to update. If I had to guess, I'd imagine if you triggered reflow somehow, maybe by animating the width or setting the style attribute during animation, it would pop?

> If I had to guess, I'd imagine if you triggered reflow somehow, maybe by animating the width or setting the style attribute during animation, it would pop?

It seems to update the position on scroll & if I toggle a padding. I've updated [the demo](https://codepen.io/jaffathecake/pen/Qwyjyma?editors=1111). That's the behaviour we should target here.

So I think this does need a spec change, at the very least implicit anchor element should only be set to null once https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#remove-an-element-from-the-top-layer-immediately finishes (be that called directly or via the request mechanism). That + actually implementing overlay inside of WebKit and Firefox should provide the desired behaviour.

> actually implementing overlay inside of WebKit and Firefox should provide the desired behaviour

I don't think it's about the overlay property though; I think it's about style invalidation. The CSS spec _also_ needs updating to describe this.
In terms of the spec, what breaks if the implicit anchor element is not set to null on hide?

> In terms of the spec, what breaks if the implicit anchor element is not set to null on hide?

If you `showPopover(); hidePopover(); popover.style = 'display:block'` you'd still be anchored, when you might not want to be.
le sigh

> I don't think it's about the overlay property though

> I think it would be preferred to detect a transition and queue removal after the animation/transition cycle.

The overlay property behaviour + the spec change I mentioned would give you *exactly* that behaviour?

> The overlay property behaviour + the spec change I mentioned would give you _exactly_ that behaviour?

No because removing the anchor would still trigger reflow! You'd be on the top layer but you'd snap to the middle of the screen 😆

If you're meaning to use the "remove from top layer" queuing mechanism, like a callback, then yes.
Alright I've done the specs: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/11695 https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/pull/12850. Who wants to write the tests 😜

Do we actually want to genericize the algorithm like that? Whether a popover has an implicit anchor seems, to me, to be identical to the question of whether it has a ::backdrop or not, no? That's currently implicitly tied to whether the element is being [rendered in the top layer](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#render-in-the-top-layer), so we should just do the same for implicit anchor, yeah?

I would suggest that the implicit anchor is incidental to the `::backdrop`, or `overlay`. For example a Dialog does not have an implicit anchor, but a modal dialog has backdrop and overlay. 

In addition, to _not_ generalise means the html spec would add but never remove the implicit anchor which may lead to some level of confusion.
cc @mfreed7 @josepharhar

Sorry I hadn't seen this issue. Let me see if I understand what's been said:

a) the current spec is a bit wrong, since in the [hide popover algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#hide-popover-algorithm) step 9.5 sets the implicit anchor to null.
b) Chrome instead does that in [remove from top layer immediately](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/dom/document.cc;l=8675;drc=4ae3a738cbcbfb87d2bf747e530650484e448361).
c) that, plus the `overlay` property, maintains the desired behavior, in which the popover stays in the top layer during the transition out.

It looks like the two spec PRs above roughly do that, except that they modify [process-top-layer-removals](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#process-top-layer-removals) rather than [remove-an-element-from-the-top-layer-immediately](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-position-4/#remove-an-element-from-the-top-layer-immediately). But that's functionally equivalent.

If I've got all of that right, this looks good to me.

> If you showPopover(); hidePopover(); popover.style = 'display:block' you'd still be anchored, when you might not want to be.

This seems like a bit of an odd thing to do? Is persisting the invoker relationship until the next open really a problem?

> This seems like a bit of an odd thing to do?

I think it's possible some people will want a popover that's always visible it's just sometime static positioned in the page and sometimes in the top layer. That being said I agree it would be weird to do the above but *keep* position fixed.

I did exactly this with the superscript 7 in https://jakearchibald.com/2025/give-footnotes-the-boot/#footnotes-on-the-web.

By default it's a footnote at the bottom of the page, and when it's clicked it's popover.

But, when it's a footnote, it's position static, so the anchoring isn't an issue.
I think this can have agenda+ removed?

> I would suggest that the implicit anchor is incidental to the ::backdrop, or overlay. For example a Dialog does not have an implicit anchor, but a modal dialog has backdrop and overlay.

I didn't mean that the implicit anchor is caused by having a backdrop; I meant that both the implicit anchor *and* backdrops are caused by the same condition, which is being "rendered in the top layer". We shouldn't be manually managing these sub-states by passing around algo steps, we should just make them dependent on that state of being in the top layer. It's then the impl's responsibility to clean things up at the same time as they actually remove an element from the top layer, rather than the spec author's responsibility to very carefully manage the states.
